introduction: This level targets the natural, physical phenomena that plague high-voltage AC transmission lines. State AE/JE examiners love testing the causes and mitigation of these specific effects.

core_concepts.title: Ferranti Effect
core_concepts.description:
A phenomenon occurring in Medium and Long transmission lines under no-load or extremely light-load conditions, where the **Receiving end voltage ($V_r$) becomes strictly greater than the Sending end voltage ($V_s$)**. 
- **Cause:** The line capacitance (charging current). 
- **Mitigation:** Controlled by connecting Shunt Reactors at the receiving end.

core_concepts.title: Skin Effect
core_concepts.description:
The tendency of alternating current (AC) to concentrate and flow near the surface (skin) of a conductor rather than distributing uniformly across its cross-section. 
- **Note:** Skin effect is **ZERO in DC circuits** (DC flows uniformly). It increases with higher Frequency, larger Diameter, and higher Permeability.

core_concepts.title: Corona Discharge
core_concepts.description:
The ionization of the air surrounding a high-voltage power conductor. 
- **Symptoms:** Produces a faint luminous violet glow, a hissing noise, and generates Ozone gas ($O_3$). 
- **Disadvantages:** Causes power loss and severe Radio Interference (RI).

core_concepts.title: Proximity Effect
core_concepts.description: The uneven distribution of current in a conductor caused by the magnetic field of a neighboring, closely placed current-carrying conductor.

important_entities.name: ACSR Conductor
important_entities.significance: Because of the Skin Effect, AC mostly flows on the outer surface anyway. Therefore, we use highly conductive Aluminum strands on the outside to carry the current, and high tensile Steel strands in the core solely to provide mechanical strength.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Exam Trap: Examiners ask if the Ferranti Effect occurs in Short transmission lines (less than 80 km). The answer is **NO**. Short lines have negligible capacitance, hence no charging current, making the Ferranti effect impossible.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Skin effect increases directly with Frequency (F), Diameter (D), and Permeability (P).

exam_strategy_tips: A favorite RRB JE / SSC JE theoretical question: 'What is the phenomenon where the receiving end voltage exceeds the sending end voltage at no-load?' Answer: Ferranti Effect.
